quest.title: The Final Judgment
quest.description: You finally make your way back to the Pillar Hall from the Apathic Interval...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x400, Primogem x50, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.num: A Long Day in the Mountains: Chapter 3
chapter.title: Judgment

talks.objective: Go to the center of the Pillar Hall

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Wow, you really do wind up seeing anything if you live long enough...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I was just thinking earlier — you were incredible back there, especially against Melanta... but...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: What was it you did again?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: And... who are you, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is your memory fading away?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Who... am I?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your name is Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #That's right! Also, Paimon's Paimon, and this here is {NICKNAME}. We're your good friends!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Friends...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes! We're friends who've been through hell and back together.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Really?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I can feel it. It must be true.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And your sister's been traveling the world lately, just to clear her head. Someday, the two of you will meet again.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She might not remember you at first, either... but you share the same blood, not to mention the same face.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You'll recognize each other right away, Paimon's sure of it!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I have an older sister...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, you can ignore this gravestone!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Your sister put it up herself, just for fun. It's her way of saying she's been reborn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's definitely still alive!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: My sister...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mm-hmm.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: She's kind of silly, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Anyway, there should be some information about you in your suitcase. Take a look. You'll probably remember things once you do.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Okay. I will.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And one more thing. You're an amazing person.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Like, saved-an-entire-world amazing.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Who, me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everyone is deeply grateful to you. So live proudly, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And if anyone ever picks on you or makes you feel bad, just write to {NICKNAME}. There's nothing {F#she}{M#he} can't handle for you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything you want to do right now?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I don't know... But I'm... starving. Like I haven't eaten in days.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Heh. Paimon's hungry too! She needs food now!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hurry up and empty your backpack! Paimon wants tons of Chicken-Mushroom Skewers!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Lind... I can't let you return to the human world like this.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: And yet, once again, I stayed silent out of cowardice.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: If you go back to the mortal world this way... I know what choice you'll make.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: We've said all we needed to say. That's all this is.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What are you talking about? Paimon doesn't get it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Weren't we talking about how we can manifest the Path to the Heavens and then teach Melanta a lesson?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The one who went to face Melanta for all of us...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The one who gave up every last memory... was your sister, Lind.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: What...?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Back then, the early signs of Melanta's madness had begun to surface, and many suffered for it.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: After all, we are not machines, and with lives that stretch on without end, that which we forget will always find its way back.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: She heard of Melanta's increasingly unreasonable tyranny, saw the many souls who had been cast down by his judgments.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I told her to treat everything here as nothing more than an unpleasant glimpse of paradise.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: No need for anger, no need for sorrow. Since she, too, had been sent up here by Nihilita, Dex could always send her back.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: And what would it change, returning just as she was?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: That's exactly what she said as well. Haha, you two really are alike.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I've heard that many times before.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: But she was bright and talkative. You are reserved, steady.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: That's what many people say, too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, you said this before, didn't you? With the god of the Temple of Space gone, the Path to the Heavens won't vanish after it's been used once.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... are we supposed to take the path Zeitlind's sister left for us?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: If that was the case, then my tactical advice would be simple: We rush in and beat the stuffing out of him.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: No one knows what Melanta said to Hilda. But afterward, in a fit of rage, he severed the Path to the Heavens that had been formed from your sister's memories.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: And Hilda has already left this place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then... doesn't that mean someone has to give up all their memories again to get us up there?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey... what about Dex?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Isn't it the same species as that baddie? If Melanta can go back and forth, then maybe Dex could do it too if it tried hard enough!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The space separating the Atrium of Suchness at its highest from the Hall of Emptiness is called the Corridor of Nothingness...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The Corridor's power comes from the temple itself. It is the rule of departure, while the Watchers exist to uphold that rule.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Dex is only an immature Watcher, and lacks the authority to control it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, but then what can we do?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I'll offer up my memories.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I've said it before, this happened because of my cowardice. The truths I know, the history, the knowledge... They are too heavy to bear.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I hesitated, and Hilda saw right through me.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Compared to you, the suffering of an ordinary human life really must seem like a negligible price.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, no, absolutely not. Everyone says you're a treasure to humanity. Let someone else do it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #But {NICKNAME} and Paimon... Uh, we still have some important things to take care of...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's not right, Paimon. Everyone is equal.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Bearing great responsibility is no reason to sacrifice others.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And going around asking who's willing to give up everything they've lived through... That doesn't feel right either.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Let me do it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zeitlind!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: You're saying the exact same thing your sister did. But this time, I absolutely refuse to accept it.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: You've been here witnessing history across the ages, seeing every wonder this world has to offer.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: After all that... doesn't even a tiny part of you feel attached to this world?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I think I finally know the answer to that question now — that most fundamental question of philosophy, which is whether one chooses to go on living tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: You hesitated. And even that brief pause is enough to show the answer is already there: tomorrow is worth living through.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: No, Istoria. Wise though you are, you've made two mistakes.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Enlighten me, please.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Why did Nihilita choose my sister?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: And was it really just coincidence that I was brought here?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Your sister said it herself — it was just a coincidence.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The sanatorium had announced its closure, but before the relocation, she went for a walk at midnight... and that's when she encountered Nihilita.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: It wasn't an accident. Listen, when you save yourself, you save the world entire.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: But...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: If my sister hadn't lost everything she once remembered, she would never have chosen to go on living.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Now I understand why I was always sure she was still alive. A life that begins anew is full of hope, surely?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: And here I recall a passage I once read in a novel by Karasawa Eichi:

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: "The savior offers themself in a world of darkness, willingly bound upon the cross. Only then is their soul redeemed, ascending into the kingdom of light."

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Isn't that incredible? It means you can heal your own melancholy and save the world at the same time.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: So, I'm not giving that chance to you.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Ah...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: For a second, I almost thought that was Hilda talking. But that's not really her style.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Of course not. She doesn't read much — she couldn't quote the classics half as well as I do.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: #Paimon, {NICKNAME}, you're not allowed to object either.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: When I return to the world below with my memories gone, I'll need you to tell me who I am — and where I'm meant to go.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! How are we supposed to respond to that!? We've only just met, and you're already talking about erasing everything and starting over like none of this ever happened...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: "A story so good you'd forget everything just to experience it again" — that's the highest praise there is. You're friends of that caliber, I'd say.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, thanks for trying to lighten the mood, but... Paimon's still getting all teary-eyed...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: So, Istoria... Please take us there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is there anything else you need to do?

choices.text: Give me a few moments more to prepare.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: I'll wait for you. Let us bear witness together when the time comes.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: This is... my sister's handwriting.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, are these letters we didn't manage to collect down below earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: No. Just a few messages she left behind, and a short poem she wrote.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: It's not a farewell. She must still be alive.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can we read all this?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Oh, you will.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You arrive at the upper level...

talks.objective: Build the stairway to the heavens

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: May I try to persuade you one last time, Zeitlind?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Your argument has already failed, Mr. Istoria.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: My sister's grave down below is empty. Aren't you worried I might just leave now and lie down in it myself?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: ...Alright.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The stairway to the heavens manifested from your sister's memories was severed, but part of it should still remain.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: This time, your memories might intertwine with Hilda's, which might cause something unique to manifest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So does that mean Zeitlind might still keep half her memories?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I explained this before. Offering up all one's memories has nothing to do with passing through the Corridor of Nothingness.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Allowing you one final glimpse back... That is merely an act of mercy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh wait, then won't we end up seeing some really private stuff? Uh... is it okay for us to go along too?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: "I offer you the memory of a yellow rose seen at sunset, years before you were born."

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: "I offer you explanations of yourself, theories about yourself, authentic and surprising news of yourself."

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: You'll still have to answer every question about me, you know.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: So feel free to look. These will prove indispensable in rebuilding the real me.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: If it concerns her privacy, then we'll watch it together. Hmph, leaving her little sister to wander the world alone? She had it coming.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Never mind trying to talk tough... Now you sound like you're just being mean...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And look at you — suddenly so chatty, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Is that so?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Are we building the Corridor of Nothingness's stairway to the heavens right here?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Yes.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Then let's begin.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: My sister's poem...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Oh my. It's all emotion. Not a lick of literary flair.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Still, it's not bad.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you still remember who we are, Zeitlind?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Hey, Istoria already said my memories will only fade quickly once we leave this place.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: So I know exactly who you are... and who I am.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: What I just saw... was all the worlds my sister used to read out to me when we were kids. The worlds we dreamed of together.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Are there really sunken treasures beneath Fontaine's high seas? Are there really youkai in Inazuma's Chinju Forest?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Do magical spirits like the Aranara really exist in this world? Have I grown up too much to ever see them again?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The Aranara do exist! And they draw power from people's memories.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Then I must be an Aranara too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've already seen things far more wondrous than that. They do exist.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I'd love to see the Aranara someday.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: From now on, the Path to the Heavens linking the Hall of Emptiness and this tower...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: They will exist only as two girls' shared longing for a beautiful world.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: That, too, is a kind of eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Well, are you ready?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Lind... Would you reconsider?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: No.

response.speaker: Zeitlind
response.text: I'll wait for you. Let us bear witness together when the time comes.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Outlander... Since you are no child of humanity, how should I address you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #My name is {NICKNAME}. And...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean by "child of humanity"?

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: All who descend from the first ancestor shaped by the lord of all, and those born of that lineage, are called children of humanity. Even the artificial people of the Primordial Sea, granted special pardon, are counted among them.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: But you... You stand outside this order.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #Why did a god take my {M#sister}{F#brother}?

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: I cannot answer, because I do not comprehend it myself.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: I once believed it was merely punishment for transgressions. But now I fear there is a deeper meaning behind it, as it is with the heretical myth that light and darkness birthed the primordial human.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why are you suddenly answering all our questions so readily?

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: This is a rule engraved upon my very soul. When a human child offers up everything in pursuit of an answer, I must speak in the Creator's stead, and withhold nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: In the end, that human child will forget all things. Fleeting answers, eternal release — this too is an expression of divine mercy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then why are you being so harsh to the people in the Hall of Emptiness?

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: This, too, is law. With the Creator absent and Nihil fallen from grace, I must uphold the measure once set by my lord.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: This place exists only to preserve. All innovation, all evolution, is forbidden here.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: If I remember correctly... your name is Melanta, right?

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: I know your name, human child.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: How did my sister speak of me to you?

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: She said that she and I could never reach accord, but that one day, her younger sister would come and defeat me.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Did you hear that? In the end, you're the ones who were dragged into this — victims in my conflict.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. So we really were just hired muscle, chasing a bit of pay. That Nihilita, seriously...

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Nihilita... The traitor, the Fallen One!

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: He abandoned his charge, yet dares to proclaim himself enlightened!

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: We Watchers were meant only to stand in silence, keeping vigil here, at the Pillar Hall of the World.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You got worked up all of a sudden. Guess you're the type to get all sulky to see someone else free while you're stuck.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: But my sister miscalculated in one way.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I'm an introvert. I'm not good with words. I've read a lot, sure. Maybe I even understand plenty of truths.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: But I avoid talking when I can. The one who'll change your mind isn't me.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}... I'll leave it to you.

talks.objective: Go to the Corridor of Nothingness

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Child of humanity... No... You are...!

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: #My creator, my lord... why would you choose {F#him}{M#her} and abandon me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, did it... suddenly fly into a rage...?

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Send them back.

talks.objective: Find the hidden enemies and defeat them
Find the hidden enemies and defeat them
Find the hidden enemies and defeat them
Find the hidden enemies and defeat them

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Nihilita! Nihilita!

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: I understand. I understand now...

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: When the divine departs the throne, all creations are free.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Melanta.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: What do you want to say?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: This comes from years of living alongside my own melancholy, though I suppose I'm saying it a bit late.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: If your melancholy feels uncontrollable, that's a physiological illness. You should seek help early. Get treatment, and cooperate with the ones administering it.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: You are like your sister. Utterly incomprehensible.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Heh. Creatures like us — manifestations of the rules... Who shall we see when we fall ill?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Do you feel guilty now, beating up a patient?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess getting to know others has changed you a bit, Zeitlind. You sure have picked up some bad habits along the way...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: We introverts are all a little twisted on the inside.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: You won't be seeing me like this for much longer anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There you go again, saying something super saddening...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Like I said, I've got a dark side.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Melanta, I still have questions.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Then ask them now. I won't be here much longer.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Passing judgment on the painter who defiled the laws of space, severing the path to the Corridor of Nothingness...

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Those were acts of transgression. My rebellion has triggered self-destruction as per the rules themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: In truth, I would rather not answer your questions, but I suspect even that small act of defiance would only hasten my disappearance.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About my sibling...

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: You've already come this far, have you not? Your will is still your own, and your feet are still unshackled. Go, find your sibling yourself!

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: You're not like me... a being who bound their own wings, only to watch them break.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why are you tormenting everyone?

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Tormenting them? No. I'm correcting them. I'm returning them to the form heaven intended. They ascend to heaven, yet reject its sacred stillness and cling instead to the corruption of the mortal world.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: So that's it. I'm jealous. Jealous of them. Jealous of the fallen Nihilita. Jealous of change. Jealous of freedom. Jealous of... life.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: I thought that if I did everything right, then when my creator returned, she would praise me. That would have been enough. Enough to soothe me... enough to prove them all wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Why would she not look back? Why did she not ask if I wished to leave beside her...?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: If you were always this stubborn and heartless, the answer shouldn't be hard to grasp. If you'd shown even a hint of rebellion, she might have taken you with her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Zeitlind, is there anything you wanted to ask?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Me? Let me think... I want to know why people say this sanatorium is cursed.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: ...Once, the Abyss brought disaster to this land. The knights stationed here fought to the last and did not retreat. When the report of the battle arrived at Dornman Port, it contained only a single line:

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: "None who went to Windrest Peak returned."

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I see. So, there never was a curse — only warriors who fell in battle and slumber on — the peak where the "knights of the west wind" rest...

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: My time is almost gone. I am filled with hate — hate for all of you. And still, I want nothing more than to cling to consciousness, to let my awareness live on, unbroken.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: You and your sister — mortals who love everything and everyone — you still yearn for an ending. And I, who want so badly to go on living... I must face mine instead.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Nihilita, my weariness runs deeper than words...

talks.objective: Return to the center of the Pillar Hall

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We taught Melanta a lesson, Istoria!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Indeed. Looking at the sky tells me as much.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Did Melanta say anything useful?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Istoria what just happened...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: *sigh* The word "Watcher" originally referred to those who are awakened and enlightened.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: A Watcher who closes their eye can only be swallowed by darkness. Yet awakening itself defies the Creator's will — and is thus condemned as a fall from grace.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Speaking of which... Dex. We taught you, played with you, took good care of you. You were raised by all of us together.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: When you grow up... Remember the kindness we've shown you, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way... that heretical myth about light and darkness birthing the primordial human... Do you have any idea what it refers to?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I'm not entirely sure what Melanta meant, either. The first thing that came to mind was a parable once condemned as heresy by the angels.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: It tells of the god of light who created a body in its own likeness, only for it to be stolen away by the king of darkness.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Thus, within that single body, the powers of light and darkness began to contend with one another. And so the primordial human, bearing both, came to possess both good and evil.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: It's a lesser-known version of the primordial human myth.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's... a bit too bare-bones. Not sure it'll help us much.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: And I'm afraid I cannot recall much else about this at the moment...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Aren't you going to say goodbye to me, Istoria?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I owe you an apology. And your sister, too.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Actually, while I was quiet earlier, I was thinking about something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What was it?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: What my epitaph should say.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Don't get the wrong idea, Paimon. We're not immortal, after all. Everyone needs one eventually.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: But I couldn't think of anything before. My sister's fake tombstone already had such a good line, you see.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Then, just now, it came to me.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: And?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: My epitaph will read: "To be continued."

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Pretty much on par with "One lifetime doesn't count," wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: A person is a story in motion. It shouldn't end just because life does.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: So... goodbye, Istoria.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Goodbye, Lind. And when you see Hilda, give her my regards.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I can't promise I'll remember any of this. And I can't promise she'll remember you, either.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: #Come on, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. Take me back down. Then... we'll meet again, like it's the first time.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Nihilita! Nihilita!

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: I understand. I understand now...

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: When the divine departs the throne, all creations are free.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Melanta.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: What do you want to say?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: This comes from years of living alongside my own melancholy, though I suppose I'm saying it a bit late.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: If your melancholy feels uncontrollable, that's a physiological illness. You should seek help early. Get treatment, and cooperate with the ones administering it.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: You are like your sister. Utterly incomprehensible.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Heh. Creatures like us — manifestations of the rules... Who shall we see when we fall ill?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Do you feel guilty now, beating up a patient?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Guess getting to know others has changed you a bit, Zeitlind. You sure have picked up some bad habits along the way...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: We introverts are all a little twisted on the inside.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: You won't be seeing me like this for much longer anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There you go again, saying something super saddening...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Like I said, I've got a dark side.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Melanta.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I still have questions.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: I no longer have the strength to answer them. Nor the will.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Passing judgment on the painter who defiled the laws of space, severing the path to the Corridor of Nothingness...

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Those were acts of transgression. My rebellion has triggered self-destruction as per the rules themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Melanta
dialogues.text: Nihilita, my weariness runs deeper than words...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: You arrive at the Corridor of Nothingness...
